newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal copper strike enters third day.
newsitem.headline: Portugal copper strike enters third day.

text.p: Activity at the Neves Corvo copper mine in southern Portugal was paralysed for the third day running on Wednesday as miners continued their strike over working hours, a senior company official said.
Raul Araujo, personnel director at the mine, said pickets were continuing to bar entry to employees wishing to work at the 107,000 tonnes per year mine, some 250 km southeast of Lisbon.
Miners had voted on Tuesday to continue their action in protest at plans for Sunday working.
"The impasse remains," Araujo told Reuters, adding that there were no immediate plans for further meetings between management and unions.
A meeting on Tuesday, brokered by the civil governor of nearby Beja, had ended with no progress made towards settling the dispute at Europe's largest copper mine.
Araujo said pickets were continuing to allow access only to technical and maintenance teams. "Nothing is being produced," he said.

Miners leaders had said on Tuesday that pickets were only blocking entry to the installations by side entrances and that anybody wanting to report for work through the main gate was being allowed to do so.

Beja governor Antonio Saleiro had warned unions on Tuesday that barring access to the premises was illegal and that police would be sent in if pickets prevented other employees wishing to work from turning up for their shifts.
